title: PPK sensitivity across latency bands — Hosted API tradeoffs (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, shareable spreadsheet to explore per-prompt token (PPK) sensitivity against latency buckets and infra choices (GPU family vs CPU/TPU fallbacks) across regions. This is a working scratchpad — assumptions are intentionally explicit so reviewers can poke numbers.

High-level question:
- For a given model family + region, how much margin do we lose/gain by tightening latency SLOs (e.g., p50<100ms vs p50<250ms) when we factor in instance-choice, caching, and amortized infra licensing?

Sheet layout (tabs):
1) README — overview, assumptions, change log (this tab)
2) BASE_CASE — row-per-model/region/latency-band with raw inputs and formulas
3) SCENARIOS — toggles for cache hit, quantization, burst reserve mix, spot vs reserved
4) SUMMARY_BY_LATENCY — aggregated PPK and margin heatmaps by latency slice
5) NOTES_AND_ACTIONS — quick ops/product recommendations and open Qs

BASE_CASE tab columns (example rows shown below):
- model_family: redwood-7b, redwood-14b, generic-13b
- region: us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1
- instance_type: a100-80gb, h100-80gb, gpus-rtx-48gb, c6i-large (cpu-fallback)
- base_ppk (USD): explicit base per-token infra amort estimate before cache (numbers are amortized infra + energy + licensing / expected tokens)
- latency_band: p50<100ms | p50 100-250ms | p50>250ms
- p50_ms: measured or target median latency
- p95_ms: measured or estimated p95
- cache_hit_rate: expected prefix/KV cache hit (0.0-0.9)
- effective_ppk_formula (text): base_ppk * (1 - cache_hit_rate) * model_multiplier + amort_per_request
- model_multiplier: multiplier for larger models reflecting memory/compute inefficiency (e.g., 1.0 for 7B, 1.9 for 14B)
- amort_per_request (USD): small fixed per-request cost (load, routing, metadata)

Example rows (BASE_CASE):
1) redwood-7b | us-east1 | a100-80gb | base_ppk=0.00095 | latency_band=p50<100ms | p50_ms=85 | p95_ms=210 | cache_hit_rate=0.24 | model_multiplier=1.0 | amort_per_request=0.00003 => effective_ppk ≈ 0.00095*(1-0.24)*1.0 + 0.00003 = 0.00076
2) redwood-14b | us-east1 | a100-80gb | base_ppk=0.00185 | latency_band=p50 100-250ms | p50_ms=160 | p95_ms=380 | cache_hit_rate=0.18 | model_multiplier=1.9 | amort_per_request=0.00004 => effective_ppk ≈ 0.00185*(1-0.18)*1.9 + 0.00004 = 0.00284
3) redwood-14b | ap-southeast1 | h100-80gb | base_ppk=0.00210 | latency_band=p50<100ms (aggressive) | cache_hit_rate=0.12 | model_multiplier=1.9 | amort_per_request=0.00006 => effective_ppk ≈ 0.00210*(1-0.12)*1.9 + 0.00006 = 0.00344
4) generic-13b | eu-west1 | cpu-fallback | base_ppk=0.00350 | latency_band=p50>250ms | cache_hit_rate=0.05 | model_multiplier=1.6 | amort_per_request=0.00010 => effective_ppk ≈ 0.00350*(1-0.05)*1.6 + 0.00010 = 0.00541

Scenario toggle examples (SCENARIOS tab):
- HIGH_CACHE: increase cache_hit_rate +0.15 absolute (simulate large prefix reuse workloads)
- QUANTIZED: apply model_discount_multiplier of 0.65 to base_ppk for quantized kernels (model perf regression risks noted)
- RESERVE_MIX: reserved vs spot pricing blend alters base_ppk by region (e.g., asia premium +18%)
- LATENCY_TIGHTEN: force service to prefer lower-latency instance class (move rows from a100 -> h100 or to higher-cost tiling) and recompute p50/p95 and ppk impact

Aggregations (SUMMARY_BY_LATENCY):
- For each latency_band, compute weighted avg effective_ppk (weights = token volume provided in separate column) and gross_margin assuming list_price_ppk (example list price = 0.0035 USD for 7b-latency-SKU)
- margin = list_price_ppk - effective_ppk; margin_pct = margin / list_price_ppk

Quick sensitivity findings from scratch numbers (high-level):
- Tightening p50 from ~160ms to <100ms for 14B in us-east1 (forcing higher-end GPUs) increases effective_ppk by ~18–30% depending on cache assumptions. If list price is fixed, gross margin on that slice falls by ~9–15 percentage points.
- Large cache improvements (delta +0.2 absolute) buy back ~10–30% of PPK depending on model size. For 7B shapes, cache is particularly high ROI because compute is small but repeated prefixes dominate.
- Regional premiums: ap-southeast1 shows +12–22% base_ppk vs us-east1 for same model class; latency constraints amplify the delta because fewer instance choices are cost-effective.
- CPU fallbacks look economical only for very relaxed latency bands (p50>250ms) or very low-value long-running workloads. For interactive SLOs, CPU fallback margin is usually negative vs GPU when list_price_ppk remains unchanged.

Risk notes:
- These are amortized numbers — we assume steady-state utilization (slot-fill > 70%). Short bursts or cold-start dominated workloads will have much worse PPK.
- Quantization discount assumes no large prompt-quality regressions; we need evals on critical prompt sets before recommending price/SLAs tied to quantized variants.
- Cache hit improvement assumes stable request distribution — small enterprise customers with high per-user uniqueness won’t see the same uplift.

Actionable next steps (NOTES_AND_ACTIONS tab):
- Ops: extract 90-day p50/p95 histogram per model-region-route from logs (ticket JIRA-OPS-210) — need real distributions to replace rough latency bands.
- Product: propose 2 latency-tier SKUs (interactive: p50<120ms, standard: p50~200ms) and run margin sims vs current list prices.
- Finance: sanity-check amortization assumptions (GPU license + infra) for ap-southeast1 and eu-west1; provide regional cost multipliers.
- Research: run small eval comparing quantized redwood-14b@INT8 vs FP16 on our eval set (quality delta threshold 1.5% allowed) — if pass, run QUANTIZED scenario and reprice.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we tie price-sku to p95 or p50? p95 control is much more expensive but customers care about tail. Need product/SDR input.
- How to represent burst-reserve insurance (we assume simple premium +x% for guaranteed latency under surge). Model a more realistic burst model in next iteration.

Notes on how to use the sheet quickly:
- Toggle SCENARIOS booleans in the left-most column; view SUMMARY_BY_LATENCY to see high-level PPK and margin movement; expand per-model rows to see where highest delta occurs.
- Preserve BASE_CASE raw inputs — they are the source of truth for replication.

Owner/contact: Priya Patel (product-optimize) — ping in #pricing-sim for quick review threads.
